question: Which of the following is NOT a carbon compound?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Co(NO3)2**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The compound that is **NOT** a carbon compound is **Co(NO3)2**
 
• This is because **Co(NO3)2** is cobalt nitrate, which contains cobalt (Co), nitrogen (N), and oxygen (O), but no carbon atoms.
 
• It is a salt that results from the combination of cobalt(II) ions with nitrate (NO₃⁻) ions.
 
• **Carbon compounds** (also known as organic compounds) are primarily **composed of carbon atoms**, often combined with hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, or other elements

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Carbon Compounds**

 
 
• **On the basis of a number of bonds formed between two carbon atoms in a compound, carbon compounds can be classified into two main categories:**
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Category
 Description
 Examples
 
 

 Saturated Carbon Compounds
 Compounds in which each carbon atom forms single bonds with other atoms. These compounds have the maximum number of hydrogen atoms attached to each carbon atom.
 - Methane (CH₄)

 - Ethane (C₂H₆)

 - Butane (C₄H₁₀)
 
 

 Unsaturated Carbon Compounds
 Compounds in which carbon atoms are connected by one or more double or triple bonds, leading to fewer hydrogen atoms attached to the carbon atoms.
 - Ethene (C₂H₄) (Double bond between carbon atoms)

 - Ethyne (C₂H₂) (Triple bond between carbon atoms)

 - Benzene (C₆H₆) (Aromatic compound with alternating double bonds
